answer: In this PoA design, each identity—including labels such as karst, velvet, and oasis—must complete a fixed chain of modular squarings, with each result required to compute the next. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the completed work efficiently. GPUs may process separate clone chains in parallel, but they cannot remove the dependency-bound elapsed time for any individual chain; multiplying identities therefore still requires real time and computational resources.
